_about: REQ-MDL-1/1a/2. The fixed built-in archetype library. Definitions live here,
under source control and covered by golden vectors, never inline in component code.
`archetypes` is a literal GSSK archetypes block: it is spliced into a model
unchanged and validates against gssk.schema.json. `library` is application
metadata keyed by the same names and is deliberately OUTSIDE the model, per
REQ-KERN-2 — the application never smuggles its own keys into model JSON.
expense_category is deliberately absent. It was draft v0.1's single expense
primitive and it encoded the error §2.1a corrects: an expense is not, in
general, an edge into a sink.
_wiring: Three kernel facts decide what a template may contain (GSSK v5.0.0, src/gssk.c):
- ARCH_EDGE_PARAM_KEYS is {k, threshold}. A template edge names no model node,
so it can carry neither control_node nor numerator_node.
- ARCH_EDGE_KEYS excludes forcing. A template edge cannot be forced.
- Expansion rewrites BOTH endpoints to `{instance}__{member}`, so a template
edge cannot reach anything outside its own instance.
Any edge needing forcing, a control_node, or an external endpoint is therefore
emitted by the model builder after expansion. `library[name].wiring` is the
declaration of what the builder owes each instance.
Port order is load-bearing: the kernel takes default_in from the FIRST entry of
`ports` and default_out from the LAST, by insertion order. It never reads the

income_stream._purpose: Salary, rent, dividends. `flow` is the builder-emitted outgoing edge, not a member: it must reach an account outside the instance and it must carry forcing, and a template edge can do neither.

purchase_to_stock._purpose: Groceries, toothpaste, fuel. Transaction diamond whose real leg terminates in a household store named by the instance (REQ-MDL-1a) — the archetype holds no stock of its own, so two items buying into one pantry share it.

edges._leg: goods in — the counterparty supplies the transaction
money out — payment crosses the boundary into the counterparty's system

purchase_consumed._purpose: Electricity, rail fares, a haircut. Consumed on receipt, so the real leg terminates in a dissipation sink rather than a store.

edges._leg: goods in — the counterparty supplies the transaction
money out — payment crosses the boundary into the counterparty's system
the real leg, used up on receipt — REQ-FLOW-0: a diamond leg carries no logic and no params, the exchange node computes it

transfer_expense._purpose: Tax, interest, insurance premiums, bank fees. The one expense shape that really is an edge into a sink: money out, nothing back, no exchange node.

consumable_item._purpose: Toothpaste, pantry goods. Stock depletion — the fourth expense shape, in which no money moves.

edges._leg: depletion — linear for use proportional to stock on hand

durable_asset._purpose: Car, appliance, laptop. Two coupled stores: book_value on money and condition on material. ADR 4 as amended — book_value holds the DEPRECIABLE BASE (value minus salvage), so a single linear edge decays asymptotically to zero and the displayed book value is asymptotic to salvage exactly. No threshold floor, and no second edge off the same store to double-count.

edges._leg: declining-balance depreciation of the depreciable base
physical wear — a different sink class from depreciation, never summed with it

income_asset._purpose: Rental property, share parcel. Holds recoverable value and produces cashflow.

edges._leg: depreciation of the body, on the depreciable base as durable_asset does

liability._purpose: Mortgage, card, loan. ADR 3 — daily accrual, monthly payment. `interest_accrued` is a constant pinned at 1.0 and exists only to be the ORIGIN of the interest edge: REQ-FLOW-2 forbids a self-edge, so interest is `interaction` logic with the principal store as control_node. That edge needs a control_node and is therefore builder-emitted, not a template edge.

edges._leg: principal retired by payment — flows only while principal exceeds the threshold

wiring.note: The pay cycle is a forced waveform, and forcing cannot live on a template edge. §4.1: a fixed recurring bill is `constant` with `forcing`, and income is the same shape with the sign reversed.
REQ-FLOW-0: a diamond edge carries no logic and no params. The exchange node computes both legs from its own k and price.
REQ-MDL-1a: the instance names the household store its real leg terminates in. Two instances naming the same store share it.

purchase_consumed.limitation: Ships on the material carrier only. Electricity belongs on the energy carrier, and REQ-ONT-10 forbids merging carriers, so an energy variant is deferred rather than folded in here. See p0a-purchase-consumed-energy.

wiring.note: Money out with no real leg — the only expense shape with no exchange node. Recurrence is a forced waveform, so the edge is the builder's.
The yield reaches an account outside the instance, so the edge is the builder's.

REQ-FLOW-2: never a self-edge. Constant pinned at 1.0 as origin, interaction logic, principal as control_node — read, never consumed. F = k · 1 · Q_principal = dailyRate · principal. A template edge cannot carry control_node, and control_node does not resolve composite ids, so the builder names the expanded id directly.
The monthly payment. ADR 3 pairs it with daily accrual.
